clue.text: Pit strike — wartime leader disregarded one course for consumers

parts.note: a pit is a mine, as in a coal pit

indicators.note: the commander's nickname is ignored, so those letters drop out of the word for hit

parts.note: to strike is to hit, the word itself taken here
Ike was the nickname of Eisenhower, the Allied commander in the Second World War
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coal strike coincides with a wartime leader being ignored, and somebody serves a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wartime leader disregarded' removes IKE (General Eisenhower) from STRIKE, leaving STR between MINE and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian vegetable soup is a dish served as one part of a meal to those eating it.

clue.text: The staff came out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Employees walked out of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial club carried as a symbol of office is a staff borne before an official.

clue.text: The number right in the corner

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: The figure is correct in that corner of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small recess or secluded spot is a corner of a room.

clue.text: Mat is up, so is Lucy, giving the impression: something is wrong

annotationWithheld.why: Mat is up, so is Lucy, giving the impression: something is wrong (12): the anagram fodder 'is up, so is Lucy' gives all twelve letters, but no other word signals the anagram, so 'up' would be both fodder and indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Mat is up, so is Lucy, giving the impression: something is wrong

clue.text: Stretch out between tacks

explanation.surface: Something extends between drawing pins.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an arm is to stretch out; in sailing, a leg sailed on one course between changes of tack is also so called.

clue.text: A number go in state at night

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number

indicators.note: in places the word for go inside the abbreviated state

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California, a US state
a go is a turn, as in a board game

explanation.surface: Several people take a turn within one state after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TURN inside CAL, the abbreviation for California.
explanation.definitionFit: Active or happening after dark is the meaning, as with owls that hunt only after sunset.

clue.text: Show disapproval of a peninsula

explanation.surface: Expressing contempt toward a strip of land.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel saliva shows contempt; a narrow point of land running out into the sea is also so called.

clue.text: Able to make a nice difference in income

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for income

parts.note: profit is money coming in, income

indicators.note: making a difference to the word nice means altering its letter order

explanation.surface: Someone capable of making a pleasant change to their earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a difference' jumbles NICE into CIEN, which 'in' puts inside PROFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skilled and competent at a task is being capable, a close synonym.

clue.text: Soldiers blew up engineers, thanks to mineral

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the following words are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Troops detonated something, and the sappers were grateful for a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RE and TA together into ATER; 'blew' is simply its own letters, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottled spring water served at meals is called mineral water, from its dissolved salts.

clue.text: Bridge scrap makes someone ill-tempered

parts.note: to bridge a river is to cross it
a patch is a scrap of material

explanation.surface: A card game quarrel puts a player in a foul mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy, bad-tempered person is an old-fashioned informal term for a crank.

clue.text: Honey, take care of the doctor

parts.note: c/o, read as CO, is the abbreviation for care of on letters
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Darling, look after the physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey' looks like a term of endearment; it stands for the wax cells in a hive.
explanation.definitionFit: The wax structure of cells in which bees store nectar is a honeycomb, often sold whole.

clue.text: Greens can repeat themselves in sponsoring amendment

indicators.note: an amendment is a change, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Environmental politicians keep restating themselves when backing a change to a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Greens looks like the political party; it is vegetables, and these salad vegetables famously repeat on the eater (cause burps).
explanation.definitionFit: Young salad alliums are green vegetables known for being hard to digest and returning as wind.

clue.text: Badly hit in ruinous power cut? I could be invaluable

indicators.note: badly says the letters come out in a wrong order
something ruinous wrecks, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: During a disastrous blackout I was hit hard, yet I could be priceless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' and 'ruinous' together scramble HIT, POWER CUT and I; 'could be' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so precious no sum could buy it is priceless, beyond any valuation.

clue.text: Climbing mountains, indicated without the first sign of doubt the descent

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word for mountains is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: the Alps are a mountain range

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word for indicated goes around the letter

parts.note: shown means indicated, pointed out

indicators.note: the opening letter of doubt is taken

explanation.surface: Ascending peaks, a climber gestured confidently toward the way down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' turns ALPS into SPLA; 'without' puts SHOWN around D, the first letter of 'doubt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft's landing in the sea at the end of its flight is its final drop from the sky.

clue.text: Being humiliated, the winner doesn't show it

explanation.surface: Someone suffering embarrassment, though the victor keeps a straight face.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disgraced is the idiom's sense; read literally, a victor's expression never shows defeat.

clue.text: Supply expert with a dream

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a vision is a dream or imagined sight

explanation.surface: Provide a specialist who has an inspiring idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks set aside for future need are supplies, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: In Diana's position, create ill feeling

parts.note: Di is a short form of the name Diana, with the possessive s
a pose is a posture or position

explanation.surface: In the princess's place, one would stir up resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone unwilling or averse is to turn them against something, breeding disinclination.

clue.text: Island where one met business acquaintances initially

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
biz is slang for business, as in showbiz

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A holiday spot where somebody first encountered colleagues from work.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balearic holiday destination in the Mediterranean, famous for its nightclubs.

clue.text: Farewell to the French about to perish

indicators.note: about means going around, so the French phrase wraps the word for perish

parts.note: au is French for to the
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: Goodbye to the people of France, who are on the point of dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DIE inside AU, French for 'to the'; 'to the French' looks like part of the farewell but supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A French leave-taking used in English, literally commending someone to God, means goodbye.

clue.text: A stage in industry

explanation.surface: A step in the manufacturing process.
explanation.definitionFit: A public stagecoach of old France carried this name; separately, it means hard work and steady application.

clue.text: Excitable, like Haman

explanation.surface: Nervous, like a biblical villain.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Book of Esther, Haman is hanged on the very tall gallows he built for Mordecai.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervy and easily upset is the idiom; literally, Haman was hanged from a lofty gallows.

clue.text: Single-hearted murderer nearer to maturity

indicators.note: single-hearted means the doubled letter in the middle of the word is cut to one

parts.note: a ripper is a murderer, as in Jack the Ripper

explanation.surface: A devoted killer is getting older and wiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single-hearted' leaves only one of the two Ps at the centre of RIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is more fully developed is further along toward ripeness, a comparative.

clue.text: One's required to enter American state

definitions.text: One's required to enter American state

indicators.note: to enter means going inside, so these letters sit within the abbreviated state

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia
I is the Roman numeral for one, with the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: A traveller needs this paper to get into the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts IS inside VA (Virginia); read as a whole, the clue describes the travel document itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport endorsement letting a foreigner into a country is the document needed at the border.

clue.text: Superior to engineers, you and I used to be

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior to means placed above, so the pronoun comes first

parts.note: you and I together are we
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Ranked above the engineers, the two of us once served.
explanation.definitionFit: The past plural of the verb to be: we existed or were formerly.

clue.text: Eggs left in the ground

parts.note: ova are eggs, the plural of ovum

explanation.surface: Eggs abandoned in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil; it is THE OVAL, the London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Test cricket venue in Kennington, south London, is a sports ground by that name.

clue.text: Endanger a settlement

explanation.surface: Putting a deal at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose to danger is one sense; an agreement reached by mutual concession is the other.

clue.text: Coward's refusal to take a high line

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads Coward is

parts.note: no is a refusal
the el is an American elevated railway, a raised line

explanation.surface: A timid person declines to take an elevated route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person; it is Noel Coward, the English playwright, so the answer is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright and songwriter Sir Noël Coward bore this first name.

clue.text: The seas are rough for Viola

indicators.note: rough seas are disturbed, so these letters are churned up

explanation.surface: Stormy waters await a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viola' looks like the instrument; it is the plant genus that includes the wild pansy.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild pansy, a small flower of the violet family, carries this folk name.
